_how_to_edit: Titles and explanations for every stage on the method pages. 'points' is a bullet list (one string per bullet); an optional 'text' adds paragraphs above it (blank line between paragraphs). The keys must match the stage ids in web/api/trace.py. 'order' lists which stages each method page shows, top to bottom; a stage listed there is shown only when that run produced it (e.g. sharpening when it is switched on).

classic.title: Classic ISP
classic.subtitle: Every step is a hand-written algorithm.

learned.title: Learned ISP
learned.subtitle: One neural network does everything after the sensor.

hybrid.title: Hybrid ISP
hybrid.subtitle: Classical steps where physics is known, a small network where it is not.

photosites.title: Light on the photosites
points: The sensor is a grid of millions of tiny light buckets called photosites.
During the exposure each photosite counts the light (photons) that falls on it.
It measures only how much light, not its colour, so the raw sensor sees a grey picture.
Each count becomes a 10 to 14-bit number. These numbers are what a RAW (.dng) file stores.
Dark areas collect few photons, so they are the noisiest part of the image.

bayer.title: Bayer colour filter
points: A tiny colour filter sits on every photosite: red, green or blue, in a repeating 2×2 RGGB pattern.
So each pixel records only one of the three colours. The other two are missing.
Green appears twice in every block because our eyes are most sensitive to green detail.
That is why the raw image looks green and checkered in the close-up.

white_balance.title: White balance
points: Different light tints a scene: bulbs look orange, shade looks blue.
White balance multiplies the red, green and blue values by separate gains so white objects look white again.
The gains come from the camera's own measurement stored in the DNG (AsShotNeutral). Gray-world is the fallback when it is missing.
Using the camera's metadata instead of guessing gave +5.8 dB in our tests.
With auto exposure on, a dark photo is also brightened here by a digital gain.

demosaic.title: Demosaicing
points: Fills in the two missing colours at every pixel from its neighbouring photosites.
We use Malvar-He-Cutler: simple interpolation, corrected using the edges seen in the other colours.
Done badly, this step causes zipper edges and false colour fringes on fine patterns.
Afterwards every pixel has red, green and blue, but still in the camera's own colours.

color_correction.title: Colour correction (CCM)
points: Every sensor's colour filters see colour a little differently from the human eye.
A 3×3 colour correction matrix, built from the colour matrices in the DNG, converts camera colours to standard sRGB.
This is what makes colours look natural and consistent between phones.
Removing this step cost 2.2 dB in our tests.

gamma_tone.title: Gamma and tone curve
points: Sensor values are linear, but our eyes notice changes in dark tones far more than in bright ones.
The sRGB gamma curve brightens the shadows so the picture looks right on a screen.
A gentle S-shaped tone curve then adds contrast, like a phone camera's photo look.
This is the first stage where the image looks like a normal photo.

denoise.title: Denoising
points: Removes the grain the sensor adds, worst in dark and high-ISO photos.
Uses an edge-preserving bilateral filter: it averages only nearby pixels with similar colours, so edges stay sharp.
Its strength follows the noise level measured in this image.
Too much smears fine texture, too little leaves grain. A hand-tuned filter has to pick one.

sharpen.title: Sharpening
points: Brings back crispness lost during demosaicing and denoising.
Unsharp masking: the difference between the image and a blurred copy is added back, on brightness only.
The amount is reduced when the image is noisy, so the grain is not sharpened too.

pack.title: Packing the four colour planes
points: The RAW mosaic is split into four half-size planes: R, G, G and B.
Each plane holds photosites of one colour, which is an easy shape for a neural network to read.
Nothing else is given to this model: no white balance, colour matrix or noise level from the file.

network_e2e.title: End-to-end network
points: A single neural network (a NAF-UNet with 2.65 million parameters) does every remaining step at once.
It learned white balance, demosaicing, denoising, colour and tone from pairs of noisy RAW photos and clean reference photos (SIDD).
It must guess the colour of the light and the camera's colours from the pixels alone.
That guessing is why its colour error (ΔE) is higher than the hybrid's.

noise_map.title: Noise map
points: Predicts how noisy every pixel is, using the camera's noise model (the DNG's NoiseProfile, or an estimate when it is missing).
Brighter pixels have more photon noise, and a higher ISO adds more on top.
This map goes into the network as a fifth input, telling it where to clean harder.
Brighter colours in the heat map mean noisier pixels.

network_hybrid.title: Network: joint denoise + demosaic
points: A small network does only the hard part: removing noise and filling in the missing colours together.
Input: the white-balanced four colour planes plus the noise map. Output: clean, full-colour linear RGB.
Doing both at once avoids the errors of doing them one after the other.
The default model is 0.7 MB (8-bit weights), trained to copy a larger teacher model. Switch to the teacher in Advanced.
